description: Which event kinds each viewer surface deliberately does not render, and why. Enforced by TestEveryEventKindReachesEveryViewerOrSaysWhyNot in internal/clichat, driven by agent.AllEventKinds (itself checked against the parsed source of the constant block). An undeclared kind that produces nothing FAILS. A declared kind that DOES produce something also fails, so a stale entry cannot hide the next real gap. Adding a kind to internal/agent therefore forces a decision on every surface instead of a silence on some of them.

tui.description: internal/uiadapter translation into the uievent stream the TUI renders.

ignores.step: An iteration boundary. Opt-in through TranslateOptions.ShowIterationNotices, which is off by default, so the ordinary transcript is not one notice per loop step.
ignores.cache_usage: A per-step prompt-cache hit rate. Opt-in through TranslateOptions.ShowPromptCacheNotices; the statusline carries the session total.
ignores.heartbeat: A wall-clock tick with no content of its own. The spinner and the statusline already say the turn is alive, and a transcript row per tick would bury the turn.

json.description: The local NDJSON stream written by --json line mode (jsonTurnEventCallback).

ignores.assistant: The answer DOES reach this surface, through ndjsonChunkWriter as chunk lines rather than through the event callback. It is declared here because the callback is what this table drives; the chunk path has its own tests.
ignores.tool_pending: An approval request. Line mode does not run an approval UI, so a consumer has no way to answer one. KNOWN GAP: a consumer therefore cannot tell that a turn is blocked waiting for approval.
ignores.heartbeat: A wall-clock tick with no content.
ignores.prune: Context pruning accounting. The compaction line carries the durable record.
ignores.tool_parallel: A batching note about calls that each get their own tool_start and tool_end.
ignores.work_limit: The soft wrap-up notice. Observability only; the instruction itself travels inside the provider request.
ignores.schema_retry: A subagent about to re-enter for schema repair. The assistant_reset that accompanies it is what a consumer must act on, and that IS emitted.
ignores.empty_response_retry: A bounded retry after an empty provider response, paired with an assistant_reset the consumer acts on.
ignores.unacted_continuation: A bounded continuation after a turn announced work and called no tool. Observability only.

relay.description: The cross-process NDJSON surface (external_* types) written by renderExternalEvent. A kind must ALSO be in hub.RelayedKinds to reach here at all - TestTheRelayAllowlistAndItsRendererAgree holds the two halves together.

ignores.tool_pending: Approval belongs to the process that owns the terminal. A second process cannot answer it, and showing it there invites a reader to wait for something they cannot do.
ignores.hook: The hub is a ONE-WAY peer relay with no input path, and a hook row is operator-facing detail about the machine that ran it. Note the reason is no longer "it never crosses a process boundary": chat-sync DOES send mivia.chat.v1.hook.ran to a remote viewer, deliberately, under the include-tool-io gate and carrying the hook's stdout only. This surface stays out because a peer gains nothing from it, not because the fact is unshareable.
ignores.heartbeat: A wall-clock tick with no content.
ignores.prune: Context pruning accounting; the relayed compaction event carries the durable record.
ignores.tool_parallel: A batching note about calls each relayed on their own.
ignores.work_limit: The soft wrap-up notice, observability only.
ignores.schema_retry: Paired with the assistant_reset that a peer acts on, which IS relayed.
ignores.empty_response_retry: Paired with the assistant_reset that a peer acts on.
ignores.cache_usage: Per-process token accounting. A peer's cost is not the reader's session cost, and mixing them makes both wrong.
ignores.token_usage: Per-process token accounting, same reason as cache_usage.
